quiz.q: What is the correct order of the four steps to apply any policy?
options: Publish spec to Exchange → create API in API Manager → add API Autodiscovery → deploy
Deploy → publish to Exchange → add Autodiscovery → create API in API Manager
Add Autodiscovery → deploy → create API in API Manager → publish to Exchange
Create API in API Manager → deploy → publish to Exchange → add Autodiscovery
quiz.explain: The same procedure works for every policy: Exchange → API Manager (instance ID) → Autodiscovery with that ID → deploy to Runtime Manager.

quiz.q: The API you want to protect has no spec in Exchange. Which option do you use in API Manager?
quiz.explain: Create new API registers the API without an Exchange spec; the class used asset type HTTP API for the simple policies-demo-app.

quiz.q: Which asset type was chosen for the policies-demo-app, which has no RAML?
quiz.explain: HTTP API is a simple API registered without RAML; a full implementation with a spec would be a REST API.

quiz.q: What does the client provider setting decide when creating an API instance?
options: Who generates client IDs and secrets for the Client ID Enforcement policy
Which space the app is deployed to
Who can see the API in Exchange
quiz.explain: The client provider (default Anypoint; Okta or Auth0 if configured by admins in Access Management) issues consumer client IDs/secrets.

quiz.q: The API instance is created but no app with its instance ID has been deployed yet. What status does it show?
quiz.explain: The status stays Unregistered until an app with this instance ID connects through Autodiscovery.

quiz.q: Which deployment property keys let the deployed app connect to API Manager?
quiz.explain: The keys need underscores. The class typed clientid, which was wrong — corrected on Day 36.

quiz.q: Where do the platform client ID and secret come from?
options: The Client ID Enforcement contract of a consumer
Access Management → Business Groups → the org → Settings
quiz.explain: They are the organization's credentials — not the client ID/secret created by the Client ID Enforcement policy. In real projects the pipeline passes them.

quiz.q: You tick "Protect value" on a deployment property and later want to see it again. What can you do?
options: Untick Protect value to reveal it
Nothing to reveal it — you can only delete it and enter it again
View it in the application logs
quiz.explain: A protected value can't be unprotected, so keep the original somewhere safe.

quiz.q: Which CloudHub 2.0 target do real organizations use, with their own load balancer and access to private networks?
quiz.explain: Shared spaces are shared with other Anypoint customers (fine for practice); private spaces are dedicated to your organization.

quiz.q: A test call to the CloudHub 2.0 app over HTTP got no response. Why?
options: CloudHub 2.0 endpoints are HTTPS by default
The app needs a proxy for HTTP
HTTP only works in private spaces
quiz.explain: On CloudHub 2.0 the app's endpoint is HTTPS by default, which is why the earlier HTTP test didn't respond.

quiz.q: Which release channel lets you pick an older runtime such as 4.4.0?
quiz.explain: Edge offers the latest, Long Term Support offered 4.6.x, and None lets you pick a specific version like 4.4.0.

cards.front: Four steps to apply any policy
cards.back: Publish spec to Exchange → create the API in API Manager (instance ID) → add API Autodiscovery with that ID → deploy to Runtime Manager.
Registers an API in API Manager without a spec in Exchange.
A simple API registered without RAML; a full implementation would be a REST API.
System that issues client IDs/secrets for Client ID Enforcement — Anypoint (default), or Okta/Auth0 if admins configured them in Access Management.

cards.front: Role of API Autodiscovery and the instance ID
cards.back: The instance ID identifies the API in API Manager; Autodiscovery uses it so the running app is linked to that API and enforces its policies.
The main flow; with APIkit, the main flow that has the Listener and APIkit Router.

cards.front: Why does the deployed app need the platform client ID/secret?
cards.back: They let the runtime authenticate to the Anypoint control plane (API Manager) so it can download policies.
Org credentials (Access Management → Business Groups → Settings) passed as deploy properties. Underscores required.

cards.front: Platform credentials vs. Client ID Enforcement credentials
cards.back: Platform ones are the **organization's** credentials for runtime ↔ API Manager; Client ID Enforcement credentials are per consumer.
A deploy property hidden like a password; it can't be unprotected — only deleted and re-entered.
Shared: shared with other customers, shared load balancer/logs — practice. Private: dedicated to your org, own load balancer, can reach private networks — real organizations.
Upload an exported jar in Runtime Manager; Studio → Anypoint Platform → Deploy to CloudHub; or a CI/CD pipeline (how real projects deploy).
Edge (latest), Long Term Support (4.6.x at the time), None (pick a specific version, e.g. 4.4.0).

cards.front: Why did the Day 35 deployment hang?
cards.back: Found on Day 36: wrong property key names (`clientid`), stray digits in the instance ID, and a name clash with a background Exchange asset.
No — the policies-demo-app had no environments or encrypted properties, so they weren't needed.
